A.evidence: Normal tissue organization; stroma, parenchyma, microenvironment, cell-autonomous and nonautonomous distinctions

B.evidence: Folkman, Shweiki, Bissell/Radisky, Dvorak, immunoediting and contextual fibroblast/vascular evidence

C.evidence: Cellular compartments, matrix structure, integrin heterodimer and endothelial architecture

D.evidence: Reciprocal signaling; fibroblast state, integrin interfaces, VEGF/endothelial response, HIF/VHL, immune context

E.evidence: Remodeling vs synthesis, oxygen-dependent dioxygenase chemistry, transport dimensions

F.evidence: Recipient dependence, signal availability, conditional feedback and response distinction

G.evidence: Fick's first law, diffusion scaling, mass balance, weighted means, relative frequency and hypothetical additive delivery

H.evidence: Published comparisons and limits: hypoxia/VEGF, fibroblast depletion, matrix crosslinking and normalization. Hypothetical readouts and causal limits

I.evidence: Normal repair, vascular development, tissue homeostasis and immune regulation

J.evidence: Defined animal-model evidence and physiological comparisons; differences among tumor and tissue contexts

K.evidence: Environmental variation, altered regulatory pathways and lineage outcomes

L.evidence: Context-dependent effects, co-option, vessel function versus density, marker limits and denominator

M.evidence: Conceptual therapeutic rationale and limits, no procedural or clinical guidance

N.evidence: Explicit 4.B.04, 4.B.05, 4.E.09 and 4.E.12 links; no repeat of detailed adhesion, immune or invasion pathways

O.evidence: 50 explained questions, 8 worked examples, 17 misconceptions, 18 recall and mastery checklist
